newsitem.title: CHILE: LatAm shares seen erratic this wk, focus on Brazil.
newsitem.headline: LatAm shares seen erratic this wk, focus on Brazil.

text.p: Investors in Latin American stocks can expect a bumpy week with markets overshadowed by fears of continued volatility in Brazil coupled with profit-taking on Wall Street, said dealers.
Only the more independent Chilean market is likely to be dominated by domestic issues as players shuffle portfolios ahead of second quarter results, they said.

"Earnings will move the market for the next two weeks. Other Latin American bolsas will have some influence, but will not be the main force," said Ida Longeri, head of research at brokerage Larrain Vial.
Mounting speculation that earnings, to be released at the end of the month, will be disappointing, is seen depressing stocks this week, they said.
The 40-share index shed 3.48 percent last week to 129.98 points as investors seized concerns over Brazil as a chance to take profits from the recent run-up in the Santiago bourse.
Brazil's Bovespa index ended last week down 15 percent at 11,182 points. At midday today, the index was up a slight 0.85 percent at 11,277 points.
In Mexico, traders said they feared volatility in Brazil and profit-taking on Wall Street could overshadow domestic fundamentals just as they appear to be improving.

"Second quarter reports are due and should be solid on the whole, and inflation data next week could provide further room to trim interest rates," said Esteban Rojas, associate reserach director at the Arka brokerage.
The blue chip IPC index zigzagged through last week to close down 2.1 percent at 4,720.56 points.
News from Brazil is also seen dominating Caracas stocks this week with few companies looking to post the kind of fundamentals warranting gains, said brokers.
"We're hoping Brazil stabilizes because if there's a collapse, it will take the rest of Latin America with it," Merinvest analyst Roberto Isasi said.
The 19-share index ended Friday down 3.7 percent at 9,1202.6 points.
Argentine stocks are seen consolidating after last week's heavy losses, although attention will remain focused on Brazil, said traders.
Analysts said stocks might pull back further in the first few days of the week, but were expected to switch back to gains by Thursday, finding technical support at 780 points.
"The undertone remains strong. What we're seeing is a healthy correction in a bullish market," said one broker.
The blue-chip MerVal index dived 5.7 percent last week to close at 802.11 points.
((-- Santiago newsroom, 562-699-5595 x212))

Sao Paulo stocks, which plunged last week on fears of a devaluation of the real, are expected to fluctuate at a much narrower range as investors adjust their portfolios to new market levels, said brokers.
"The bolsa is likely to be much less volatile than it was last week," said a senior trader.
"In the first two or three days, share prices will keep fluctuating before they stabilize," said another.
Traders said they expected sales by local stock funds and asset managers, who dominated the sell-off, to ease this week.
